rules: Reconnect never mints a new key and never replays an uncertain mutation.
A new key is minted only right after a definitive M5 refusal proving nothing was journaled: client_request_key_expired, client_request_journal_full.
M7 resubmits the exact saved key by nonce; the registry returns the accepted job or refuses.

M5 order: identical saved request -> duplicate:true; same nonce, other bytes -> client_request_key_conflict; stale namespace or epoch -> client_request_key_expired; full -> client_request_journal_full.
Registry refusals keep their existing wire spelling KeyConflict and KeyExpired.

steps.send: client writes one ControlRequest on a new owner-pipe connection
steps.reply_lost: service committed this response; the connection dropped before the client read it
steps.connection_lost_before_durable: connection dropped before M5 was durable; nothing journaled
steps.connection_lost_before_effect: connection dropped before the registry saw the submission
steps.client_mints_key: client generates caller and key; `after` names the refusal that allows it

cases.name: disconnect_before_acceptance
cases.note: The client resends the identical M5; it never mints a key because the first reply is missing.

cases.name: disconnect_before_acceptance_epoch_rotated
cases.situation: disconnect before acceptance, then stale epoch
cases.note: M5 checks the nonce before the epoch; a stale key with no journal entry is a definitive refusal, so only then may the client mint a new key.

cases.name: disconnect_after_durable_acceptance
cases.note: The resent identical M5 answers duplicate:true.

cases.name: disconnect_after_submit_reply_lost
cases.situation: disconnect after durable acceptance (submit reply lost)
cases.note: Receipt lookup recovers the accepted job; nothing is resent.

cases.name: disconnect_after_submit_not_yet_accepted
cases.note: job:null, expired:false: resend M7 with the same nonce; the saved key makes it idempotent.

cases.name: disconnect_after_completion
cases.note: A terminal receipt is displayed; forgetting never cancels work.

cases.name: client_death_before_submit
cases.note: Another surface finds the entry by M6 and submits the saved request by nonce.

cases.name: client_death_after_submit
cases.note: The new surface lacks caller and key, so it resubmits by nonce: the saved key returns the same job.

cases.name: service_restart_after_submit
cases.note: The stale instance fence refuses before dispatch; the journal and receipts are durable.

cases.name: service_restart_before_submit
cases.note: A reconnect never replays M5 with a new key.

cases.name: duplicate_key_same_arguments
cases.note: Every repeat returns the one accepted job.

cases.name: same_key_different_arguments_journal
cases.note: Fail closed; the original journal entry is unchanged.

cases.name: same_key_different_arguments_registry
cases.note: Existing registry spelling (Debug format) is kept; the original is shown by receipt.

cases.name: prepare_key_mismatch
cases.note: M5's caller and key must equal those inside its request.

cases.name: stale_epoch_journaled_not_submitted
cases.note: KeyExpired cannot distinguish never accepted from accepted and pruned (the journal records no submission), so the outcome is unknown and nothing is replayed.

cases.name: stale_epoch_already_accepted
cases.note: The accepted key is looked up before the epoch check.

cases.name: receipt_lookup_accepted
cases.note: Pending or running is accepted.

cases.name: receipt_lookup_completed
cases.note: A failed terminal outcome is completed, not unknown.

cases.name: receipt_lookup_unknown
cases.note: A pruned receipt is unknown, never success.

cases.name: management_timeout_on_submit
cases.note: The code names its own recovery: retry with the same key.

cases.name: journal_full
cases.note: Definitive refusal before journaling; inspect and forget entries, then resend.
